page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs running on 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. The architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, as well as VAES and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. System memory totals 16 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Network throughput features a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, while local instance storage is not included, requiring external block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution, driven by modern Zen-based EPYC architecture. In single-core stress-ng tests, the instance lands in the top tier, complemented by a strong single-core score of 2017.0 and high text-processing throughput in Geekbench. Multi-core performance scales predictably across its 4 vCPUs to middle-tier percentiles in stress-ng and PassMark evaluations. Conversely, memory-intensive cached operations, clang software compilation, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET throughput test in the lower quartiles. Large block uncached memory operations deliver average bandwidth, measured at 47.72 GB/sec for reads and 28.11 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g8ae.xlarge provides balanced compute and memory capacity for non-storage-intensive workloads. The lack of bundled local storage necessitates planning for attached cloud disks, which shifts I/O latency to storage volume performance. Workloads best suited for this instance type include general application servers, middle-tier enterprise services, light continuous integration jobs, and microservices requiring dedicated core isolation and high single-thread CPU performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz, it incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. The instance provides 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes. Performance profiles reflect top-tier single-core compute capabilities in stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations, balanced by middle-tier multi-core scaling. However, memory cache bandwidth and transactional database benchmarks place in lower percentiles. Given its dedicated core allocation and balanced hardware specifications, ecs.g8ae.xlarge is suited for standard enterprise applications, microservice hosting, and mid-tier backend services that benefit from consistent clock frequencies without heavy local disk I/O.
